verdicts.question: What type of roof is present at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Rooftop photos on pages 11-13 and 15 (Material Storage, Proposed PV Area, Cable Routing, Earthing Routing) all show a bare, flat, grey concrete (RCC) terrace surface with a tile-pattern finished section near the stair-head, no sloped tiled or metal-sheet roofing visible.
verdicts.rationale: Multiple independent rooftop photos consistently show a flat poured-concrete terrace, matching 'RCC Flat Roof'.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstructions on the roof that could affect the solar installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 12 'Proposed PV Area' photos and page 13/15 cable-routing photos show the proposed module zones are open, clear concrete surface. Only a small stair-head/water-tank enclosure sits in one corner, outside the marked 'Proposed PV modules' zones.
verdicts.rationale: No trees, tanks, or AC units sit within the proposed PV footprint in any rooftop photo; the one roof structure (stair head) is clearly outside the marked module areas.

verdicts.question: What is the angle of the panels? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: Structure Details renders (pages 6-8) show ballast-mounted module rows with a shallow, low-profile tilt typical of ballasted flat-roof racking, consistent with roughly a 10° angle.
verdicts.rationale: The CAD renders are schematic rather than as-built photos, but the visible tilt is shallow and consistent with the stated 10°; no contradicting evidence.

verdicts.question: On how many roofs at the site are we installing solar?
verdicts.photo_observation: Building Exterior photo (page 8) shows a single standalone building, and all rooftop photos (pages 11-16) show one continuous terrace level with all 'Proposed PV modules' labels on the same surface.
verdicts.rationale: All roof/PV-area photos depict a single flat terrace; no second roof plane appears anywhere in the documentation.

verdicts.question: What type of mounting structure is planned?
verdicts.photo_observation: Structure Details renders (pages 6-8) explicitly show modules mounted on cylindrical concrete ballast weights/pedestals with 0.50 m spacing dimensions, not rails penetrating the roof or MS/wooden framing.
verdicts.rationale: The dedicated 'Structure Details' section unambiguously depicts ballast-type pedestal mounting, matching the designer's answer.

verdicts.question: What is the orientation of the solar panels?
verdicts.photo_observation: The Site Layout schematic (page 5) shows a compass 'N' marker with module rows arranged in several different footprint directions (a horizontal row near the top, vertical columns left/right, a horizontal row at bottom), but no shading/sun arrows indicating actual panel tilt-facing direction.
verdicts.rationale: The layout is a 2D schematic of module footprint, not a photo of installed, tilted panels; the true facing direction of the ballasted tilt cannot be read from this top-down diagram alone.

verdicts.question: How can the roof be accessed?

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: DC cable (red) traced from 'Proposed PV modules' on the roof to a labeled 'Conduit' point at the parapet edge (page 13), matching a close-up photo of the actual PVC conduit and cables at that same point (page 14), then into the Inverter/UPS/Batteries diagram in the adjoining equipment room (page 14). Earthing (green) and LA (orange) cables are traced from the same rooftop modules and the stair-head LA point (pages 15-16) down through an external duct with visible bundled PVC conduit pipes and clamps (pages 17-18), terminating near the main meter board per the explicit page 18 caption.
verdicts.rationale: Each cable type (DC, earthing, LA) has a traceable, color-coded path across consecutive photo pages with labeled waypoints ('Conduit', 'Hole', main meter board) and visible physical conduit/pipe hardware at each transition; no orphan ends or unexplained gaps were found, though several segments rely on schematic overlays rather than fully as-built photos.
